title: Event-lineage re-ingestion bridge for schema-evolving analytics backfill
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reusable 're-ingestion bridge' that allows analytics backfills to reingest historical events while preserving original event lineage and safely applying schema migrations. The bridge should be resumable, shard-aware, and idempotent so downstream aggregations (BigQuery) and console dashboards do not double-count or drop metrics during partial runs.
background: We continue to see two operational pain points in console analytics reprocessing: 1) schema changes (added/renamed fields) cause ad-hoc mapping scripts and manual fixes, and 2) long-running backfills can be interrupted and restarted, leading to duplicated rows or missed windows. Existing tools (ad-hoc Dataflow jobs and one-off SQL fixes) are brittle and slow. This ticket proposes a general-purpose re-ingestion bridge that layers lineage metadata and watermark-aware checkpoints on top of our existing Kafka -> Dataflow -> BigQuery pipeline.
goals: Support schema evolution mapping rules (field rename, type coercion, defaulting) via a pluggable mapping table
Ensure idempotent writes into BigQuery by using deterministic write_keys and soft-de-duplication window
Provide resumable checkpoints per-shard/partition and a dry-run mode for validation
Expose progress and failure telemetry to Console (per-customer backfill dashboards)
non_goals: Reimplement entire historical ETL stack (we will reuse existing Dataflow runners)
Handle archiving or recovery of non-event artifacts (logs, attachments)
acceptance_criteria: Bridge can run a 30-day backfill for a single customer (50M events) and complete within SLAs without duplicating totals in BigQuery
Run can be stopped and resumed from checkpoint with identical end-state as uninterrupted run
Schema mapping rules applied to three test cases: field rename, int->string coercion, and missing-field defaulting
Console shows per-run progress, ETA, and per-partition error rates; alerts when >0.1% rows fail mapping
Integration tests and a small-scale DR run documented in Confluence (link in attachments)
design_decisions: Use Kafka consumer offsets + custom watermark file (GCS) as the canonical checkpoint store to avoid coupling to Dataflow job lifecycle
Write to BigQuery via dedup key (write_key = sha256(event_id || source_partition || original_timestamp)) and use BigQuery MERGE for finalization
Implement schema mapping as declarative YAML rules stored in Config Service with versioning for auditability
Expose dry-run mode that writes transformed events to a sandbox dataset to validate mapping before live run
implementation_notes: Create a lightweight orchestration wrapper (Dagster job) that composes: partition enumerator -> parallel Dataflow workers -> finalizer merge step
Dataflow pipelines will be parametrized with mapping version and checkpoint path; workers will tag outputs with lineage.header {original_offset, mapping_version}
Add small consumer-side TTL cache to dedupe transient duplicates produced during retries
Provide a 'repair' command that can reapply mapping to failed rows identified by error_table and re-route them through bridge
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: MERGE operations on large tables cause slot contention in BigQuery. Mitigation: stage into partitioned staging tables and shard merges by date range during off-peak windows.
Risk: Incorrect mapping rules silently corrupt historical metrics. Mitigation: require manual approval of mapping version via Console and run dry-run against sample dataset before full run.
Risk: Long-running checkpoints get garbage-collected. Mitigation: implement automatic checkpoint refresh and retention policy tied to job TTL
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Run bridge for a single low-traffic customer with 7-day window, monitor dashboard and validate totals
Phase 2: Expand to 10 customers and enable auto-retry + merge staging with throttling
Phase 3: General availability with self-serve backfill UI in Console and RBAC controls
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose metrics: processed_events, unique_write_keys, mapping_errors, resume_count, avg_checkpoint_lag
Alert: mapping_errors_rate > 0.1% for 15m -> PagerDuty; checkpoint_stalled > 30m -> Slack ops channel
Dashboard: per-run timeline + per-partition throughput charts + final reconciliation diff vs pre-run snapshot
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping engine and dedupe cache
E2E small-scale run in staging using synthetic data (10M events) and verify reconciler reports 0 delta
Chaos test: kill worker during run and validate resume semantics
Regression tests to ensure existing live streaming pipeline unaffected
open_questions: Should we support cross-region re-ingestion (EU->US) for customers with multi-region tenants? (cost + compliance implications)
What SLAs should we commit for backfill throughput for Dedicated customers vs Hosted customers?
Do we want to eventually reuse the bridge for model-serving KV cache warmups (separate follow-up ticket)
comments: 2025-01-19 - Ava Martinez: Scoped initial spike; prototyped offset+GCS checkpoint approach. Found that relying solely on Kafka consumer group offset isn't sufficient because we need stable watermark across job restarts.

2025-01-24 - Liam Chen: Prototype Dataflow pipeline implemented with mapping hook and deterministic write_key. Observed BigQuery MERGE contention when writing more than 5 concurrent shards into same partition. Added staging table plan.
